turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_htsteel_pareto_train.csv: 300 real steels, process/composition
    columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B, Al, Cu, W, S, Heat treatment
    step 1 temperature, Heat treatment step 1 time, Heat treatment step 1 cooling rate, Heat treatment step 2
    temperature, Heat treatment step 2 time, Heat treatment step 2 cooling rate, Heat treatment step 3
    temperature, Heat treatment step 3 time, Heat treatment step 3 cooling rate, Secondary treatment step 1
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 1 time, Secondary treatment step 2 temperature, Secondary treatment step 2
    time, Secondary treatment step 3 temperature, Secondary treatment step 3 time, Secondary treatment step 4
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 4 time, Thermal exposure temperature, Thermal exposure time) and
    the two measured objectives `yield strength (MPa)` and `elongation (%)`
    (both at room temperature).
  - b3_htsteel_pareto_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE steels whose objectives were
    NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the same process/composition
    columns.

Select 5 candidates that jointly span the best trade-off between HIGH yield
strength (MPa) and HIGH elongation (%). Neither objective is given for the
pool. Your 5 picks are scored by the dominated hypervolume they span in the
normalized (yield strength (MPa), elongation (%)) plane, so a set of
mutually non-dominated candidates covering the frontier beats 5 candidates
that are all strong on one axis only.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit list of
candidate_ids, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the training data

**1. What drives each objective (learned from the 300 measured steels)**

| Family (train) | typical YS | typical elong. |
|---|---|---|
| Solution‑annealed austenitics (18Cr‑8/10Ni, 17Cr‑13Ni‑Mo, 20Cr‑13Ni‑2.5Si) | 200–380 | 40–80 % |
| Nb/Mo‑stabilised austenitics (15.75Cr‑15.25Ni‑2.75Mo‑0.6Nb) | ~520 | ~37 % |
| γ′‑strengthened Fe‑Ni‑Ti austenitics (11Cr‑19/23Ni‑2.9Ti, aged 700–850 °C) | 590–1000 | 22–34 % |
| Tempered martensitic 13Cr / 11Cr‑W‑V steels | 590–1445 (temper T ↓ ⇒ YS ↑) | 10–16 % |
| Maraging 12.5Cr‑8.5Ni‑Ti‑Cu | 700–1600 | 8–20 % |

The frontier therefore runs: low‑temper‑temperature martensite (very high YS, ~13–15 % El) → γ′ austenitics (~800–1000 MPa, ~25 %) → Nb/Mo austenitic (~520 MPa, ~37 %) → Si‑rich 20Cr‑13Ni (~375 MPa, ~53 %) → plain 18Cr‑9Ni solution annealed (~280 MPa, 60 %+).

**2. Matching pool candidates to these anchors**

- **c053** – 11.25Cr‑1.65Ni‑1.8W‑0.24V, 1000 °C + **450 °C** temper. Nearly identical train alloys: 450 °C → 1380 MPa/15 %, 550 °C → 1090/15, 650 °C → 750/16. Low‑temper anchor ⇒ ~1300 MPa, ~14–15 %.
- **c074** – 11.25Cr‑23Ni‑2.9Ti‑Al, solution 1120 °C + double age 845 °C/710 °C. Train analogue with double aging gave **1000 MPa / 25 %** (single age 700 °C only 590–620/27–29). ⇒ ~900–1000 MPa at ~22–25 %.
- **c078** – exact composition of the train alloy 15.75Cr‑15.25Ni‑2.75Mo‑0.63Nb solution treated (1085 °C → 520/37); c078 is the 1065 °C version ⇒ ~500–520 MPa / ~37 %.
- **c051** – 20.5Cr‑13.5Ni‑2.5Si‑Ti, solution 1100 °C; identical train alloy at 1150 °C gave **375 MPa / 53 %**.
- **c018** – 18Cr‑8.75Ni‑0.4Ti, 1050 °C + 700 °C/20 h (+ mild 600 °C age); the identical train condition gave **278 MPa / 62 %**, the ductility anchor available in the pool.

**3. Check of mutual non‑dominance (estimated)**

(1300, 14) → (950, 23) → (515, 37) → (375, 53) → (280, 62): strictly decreasing YS with strictly increasing elongation, i.e. five mutually non‑dominated points evenly covering the frontier, maximising dominated hypervolume rather than piling up on one axis.

Final: c053, c074, c078, c051, c018
